- If sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.25) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- When model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), true outcome often overshoots and then corrects — cap forecast peak at 2–3% below true peak.
- If sentiment history includes 2+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits short-term momentum; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility bias.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment drop.
